summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 2 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.51/2493)

data.turoyo: ʕAmmo Išoʕ: Lə ḥzeli əno. Əno lə ḥzeli bale uṯewo. Uṯewo ġalabe gənwiwo. Uṯewo naqqat aḥ ḥəyewən mahzəmiwo mə qumayye, maḥəsiwo aʕlayye, rəhṭiwo, annaqqa maḥəsiwo, šuḏanwo bəṯrayye bak kefe, gurm w hay gurm (gaḥxo), bəṯrayye matəhiwonne. E hən mənayye muḥanwo bənne tfənag.
data.translation: Uncle Isho: I did not see any. I did not see any, but they would come. They would come and steal a great deal. They would come, sometimes the animals would flee from before them, they would notice them, run, then they would notice, they would rush after them with stones, bang and another bang (laughter), they would drive them away. Yes, some of them would fire guns at them.

rationale: New Infectum-wa cell with repeated third-person plural forms, including ʕal-marked target; agent transition remains uncertain.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 2 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.59/2971)

data.translation: Jan: You wouldn't notice?

summary: example for sense 2 in Infinitiv (JTM 1.2/16)

data.turoyo: Bu bayto du ʕaza, kibe naṣayəḥ, kibe qraye da kṯowe mqadše, kibe baxyo, kibe təḥiso du nsan, məqqays d foyəš bi arʕaṯe, u yawmo ḥaroyo gədəzze, huwe ste gmoyəṯ, w gdoṯən an nošanək, gəmsalən u ahəl diḏe.
data.translation: In einem Trauerhaus gibt es guten Rat, Lesungen aus den heiligen Büchern, es gibt Weinen, und dem Menschen wird bewusst, dass, wie lange er auch auf Erden verweilt, am letzten Tag auch er sterben wird, und dass die Leute kommen werden, um seine Angehörigen zu trösten.

rationale: First clear cognitive Infinitiv example; retain inherited Detransitive classification provisionally.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (MAC NE Mem and Zin/9)

data.turoyo: Maḥəsla. Kaleyo zlām bi+odayḏa damixo! Hiya lo+kəḏʕo, kəmmo, ‘Man hat, u+abro dman hat kodəmxat bi+odayḏi? Nfaq mi+odayḏi!’
data.translation: She woke up. Here’s a man asleep in her room! She does not know, she says, ‘Who are you, whose son are you, sleeping in my room? Get out of my room!’

rationale: Fourth Preterit example for sense 1: overt feminine waking event in a self-contained context.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (PrS 39/47)

data.turoyo: Nafəl u kurrəko li arʕo, tləṯ saʕat hol d maḥəsle.
data.translation: Der Jüngling fiel zu Boden und es dauerte drei Stunden, bis er wieder zur Besinnung kam,

rationale: Fifth Preterit sense-1 example distinguishes recovery from unconsciousness from sleep.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (PrS 22/17)

data.turoyo: D mamṭelən at tarte, maḥaṣle lu ʕafd w lat tartemeniye. Hawo omər: “Lox mublilox!” Qṭalle ḥḏoḏe ann arbʕo.
data.translation: Als der Riese und die Unholde erwachten, beschuldigten sie sich wechselseitig, die Mädchen weggenommen zu haben; in Folge davon gerieten die vier in Streit und tödteten sich untereinander.

rationale: Unusual maḥaṣle spelling and singular-looking agreement with a coordinated subject; preserve both.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (55/56)

data.turoyo: Hano žnu maḥəsle ʕal ruḥe, d ənnu ḥila hawi aʕle w hanək, a tre ḥaramiye, šorike ne.
data.translation: Da merkte er denn, daß man ihm einen Streich gespielt hatte und daß die beiden Diebe Kompagnons waren.

rationale: Self-awareness with ʕal ruḥe and explicit propositional content clarifies sense 2 beyond generic noticing.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (112/183)

data.turoyo: Maḥəsle henu ʕal ag garme di lašayḏe w madəqle bu tarʕo, lə ḥzele.
data.translation: Als er wieder die Knochen im Leibe spürte, Blickte er nach der Tür, sah ihn aber nicht mehr.

rationale: Somatic stimulus ʕal ag garme extends the attested noticing construction; retain ambiguity with recovery of consciousness.

summary: example for sense 3 in Preterit (6/32)

data.turoyo: I ʕamṯo kqaymo, kəmmole: "Hawi ʕaṣriye, qay lo maḥəsluxlan?" Məllela: "Anǧax."
data.translation: Die Tante steht auf und spricht zu ihm: "Es ist ja schon Abend geworden; warum hast du uns nicht geweckt?" Er spracht zu ihr: "Eben erst." (Früher ging es nicht).

rationale: Thin Preterit sense-3 cell; unusual second-person agent with first-person plural patient.

summary: example for sense 3 in Preterit (112/91)

data.turoyo: Komər l Kalaš ʕAli maḥəsle at təšʕo w tleṯi ʕabdinanək, qayimi w mədle lu sayfayḏe, falət baynaṯṯe. Qṭəʕle qarʕe dat təšʕi w tleṯi ʕavdinanək b gawa di zarzaminayo.
data.translation: Kalasch Ali weckte die neununddreißig Unholde auf; sie standen auf. Er nahm sein Schwert, fuhr zwischen sie und schnitt den neununddreißig Unholden die Köpfe ab, in jener Höhle.

rationale: Thin Preterit sense-3 cell; explicit l-marked awakener and unmarked plural awakened group.

summary: example for sense 3 in Preterit (70/262)

data.turoyo: I naqqa d hiye ṭawəʕ, hənnək maḥəsse ḥḏoḏe.
data.translation: Als er eingeschlafen war, weckte nie anderen einander.

rationale: Fills Preterit sense-3 cell to five with a reciprocal object; does not create a new sense.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (MAC NE Sterka Zera/10)

data.turoyo: Aḥ-ḥawronayḏa ṭʕənne ap-pəštiyat, aṯən lu-bayto, fayišo hiya bu-ṭuro. Fayišo bu-ṭuro, komaḥiso falge-dlalyo: k_răša hayve_k, ʕutma, falge-dlalyo.
data.translation: Her companions loaded the bundles upon themselves, they went home, but she remained behind. She remained behind, she wakes up in the middle of the night, a moonless night, darkness.

rationale: Third Infectum sense-1 example: narrative waking with explicit nighttime setting.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (PrS 78/22)

data.turoyo: Azze u taʕlo lu bayto. Mšayaʕlale laṯe du qoḏ̣e, əmmo: "Ṭro oṯe b lalyo, gmaḥtono ḥuṭo b ṣawʕi, maqəḏ̣alle bu tarʕo, ṭro oṯe u taʕlo gorašle, gmaḥəsono, soyəm aʕmi."
data.translation: Darauf ging der Fuchs nach Hause. Wiederum schickte die Frau des Richters zu ihm und liess ihm sagen, er solle zur Nachtzeit kommen, "ich will einen Faden um meinen Finger wickeln und ihn an der Türe anknüpfen; dann soll der Fuchs kommen und daran ziehen, damit ich erwache und er sich zu mir lege."

rationale: Fourth Infectum sense-1 example provides first-person feminine form gmaḥəsono.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (PrS 67/76)

data.turoyo: U taʕlo omər: "Yaman, ḥmoro, səmli məštuṯo, aṯino d qorenox, lə maḥəslox, mədli l šaqwoṯo d maḥisat."
data.translation: der Fuchs aber rief: "Pardon, Esel, ich habe einen Festschmaus veranstaltet und bin gekommen dich dazu einzuladen; da du nicht erwachtest, packte ich dich an den Hoden, um dich zu wecken."

rationale: Fifth Infectum sense-1 example provides second-person maḥisat in a purpose clause.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum (JTM 5.3/14)

data.turoyo: komər manṭalle as sakkahaṯṯe aʕmayye w manṭalle ad duquqaṯṯe aʕmayye w aṯən, məlle aydarbo gəsulqitu, mərre hawxa. komər ḥa mənayye mədle u sakka w mədle u duquqo w gum w gum w gum, kmaḥisi aʕlayye, kmahzəmi. məlle hawli, lə dayqət!
data.translation: Sie nahmen ihre Eisenpflöcke mit, nahmen ihre Holzhämmer mit und kamen (zum Schloss). Er sagte: Wie wollt ihr hinaufsteigen? Sie sagten: So. Einer von ihnen nahm einen Pflock, nahm den hölzernen Schlegel, und bum bum bum, da wurden sie auf sie aufmerksam, und sie flohen. Er sagte: Gib mir, hämmere nicht!

rationale: Third Infectum sense-2 example gives an audible trigger and ʕal-marked targets.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum (PrS 41/97)

data.turoyo: Omər: "Bayn aǧ ǧən, kətle barṯo lu malko daǧ ǧən b gawe du baḥar, kəbʕeno d gənawna, kmaḥisi aʕli."
data.translation: »Bei den Elfen, der König der Elfen hat eine Tochter mitten im Meer, die wollte ich stehlen, aber sie haben mich bemerkt«.

rationale: Fourth Infectum sense-2 example: first-person ʕal target in a complete sentence.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum (69/334)

data.turoyo: Uʕdo d maḥisi ebux", — əmmo, — "wallahi saġ gəmḥalqilux lu dəstano."
data.translation: Wenn sie dich jetzt bemerken, bei Gott, dann werfen sie dich lebendig in diesen Kessel!"

rationale: Fifth Infectum sense-2 example adds b- rather than ʕal- stimulus government.

summary: example for sense 3 in Infectum (MAC MuA Quzko/71)

data.turoyo: Məd̥ hawi lalyo, gəzzano, gmaḥəsnax’, mə́ḷḷela li+aṯto, ‘Məd daməx, ono gmādno liḏoṯe ŭ hat məd lraġloṯe, gəmḥalqínane lam+maye’. Əmmo, ‘Ăḷo haṯe mede ṭáwoyo’.
data.translation: After it becomes night, we’ll go, I’ll wake you up’, he told the woman, ‘After he falls asleep, I will take his arms and you take his legs, and we’ll toss him (lit. ‘them’) into the water’. She says, ‘Gosh, this is a good thing’.

rationale: Third Infectum sense-3 example adds explicit second-person feminine patient.

summary: example for sense 3 in Infectum (95/177)

data.turoyo: “Ya rabbi”, — omər, — “d əzzino, maḥəsno Ḥasane Aloki, gqoṭeli. Aydarbo soyamno?”
data.translation: Mein Gott, sprach er, wenn ich gehe und ihn wecke, so schlägt er mich tot. Wie soll ichs anstellen? -

rationale: Fourth Infectum sense-3 example contrasts waking another person with fear of being killed.

summary: example for sense 3 in Infectum (JTM 5.3/11)

data.turoyo: kazzi maḥəsnən, w bəṯər madna w uṯeno w qureno ay yasinat d babi, haṯe ḥaram yo gnowo yo.
data.translation: Ich gehe und wecke sie auf, erst dann nehme ich (das Feuer) und komme zurück und lese die Koransuren meines Vaters. Es wäre Sünde, ein Diebstahl.

rationale: Fifth Infectum sense-3 example; unsuffixed plural patient form complements gəm-maḥəsnən-ne already quoted.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (70/261)

data.turoyo: Ḥasan maḥiso yo, omər: "Mazal hənnək damixi, ono ste annaqqa gdomaxno! Hul d qaymi, ono ste gqoyamno." Mžədle ruḥe, ṭawəʕ.
data.translation: Ḥasan war noch wach. Er dachte: "Nachdem diese sich schlafen gelegt haben, will ich auch ein wenig schlafen. Wenn sie aufstehen, stehe ich auch auf." Er streckte sich aus und schlief ein.

rationale: Clear awake-state predicate with copula, unlike the uncertain existing ACT??? annotations.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (70/272)

data.turoyo: Komər u kurrəko maḥiso yo, kmaṣəṯ aʕlayye hawxa.
data.translation: Der Junge war wach und horchte auf das, was siesagten.

rationale: Thin awake-state cell: being awake enables listening, without a causative or concealment reading.

summary: example for sense 5 in Preterit (Jan 1.6/104)

data.turoyo: Am maḥkəyonayḏe yawmo b yawmo knəqṣi. Ġer maṯe ste, maʕəl-asaf kmaydina, a qlofe d ġer ʕame. Xaṣaṭan d Awruppa. W kmankərina u ǧawhar d kətwolan. Tawdi naqla ḥreto lu Ǧan d maḥəslelan ʕal u medano.
data.translation: Its storytellers grow fewer day by day. At other times too, unfortunately, we take the skins of other peoples, especially of Europe. And we deny the essence that we had. Thanks once again to Jan, who has made us aware of this.

rationale: First example of cognitive causation III.5, affected -lan and topic ʕal; the preceding loss of storytellers makes the topic explicit.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (Jan 3.14/141)

data.turoyo: Bi ḥarayto dann 1963 koṯən tre mḥalmoye, ḥawrone das səryoye, l gab Xori Nəʕman l Məḏyaḏ, kəmmile: "Hwawu maḥise, i dawle kəmṣalḥo a mḥalmoye w ak kurmanǧ mqabəl dəṯxu. Mṣaleḥu ruḥayxu, i niye qaṭlo, xəd u Sayfo yo."
data.translation: At the end of 1963 two Mhallami, friends of the Syriacs, come to Father Numan in Midyat and say to him: 'Be alert, the state is arming the Mhallami and the Kurds against you. Arm yourselves; the intention is killing, as in the Sayfo.'

rationale: Unusual plural maḥise under Hwawu supplies vigilance, supporting the round-1 awake-state reassignment. Hwawu is not an Imperativ of ḥys.

summary: example for sense 2b in Infectum (Jan 4.I/303)

data.turoyo: Aydarbo hawi aʕmi aw aydarbo kmaḥəsno. Kit medone, təšʕiyawoṯe hawən ḥaqiqi, təšʕiyawoṯo ste me gabi.
data.translation: How things happened to me, or how I feel. There are things whose stories happened in reality, and stories also from my own side.

rationale: Self-experience subsense 2b: how one feels contrasted with what happened, with no invented stimulus.

summary: example for sense 2b in Infectum (Jan 4.II/906)

data.turoyo: Bas hano ste, klozəm aḥna xəd ʕlaymoṯo, iḏa d maḥisina falqo mu ʕamano na, klozəm aḥna d qaymina, b ḥaylo ġalabe qawyo w mqadmina ruḥayna.
data.translation: But this too, we as young women must, if we feel we are half of this people, we must rise with very strong force and put ourselves forward.

rationale: Self-identification subsense 2b without overt ruḥo, with membership predicate falqo mu ʕamano.

summary: example for sense 2b in Infectum (Jan 4.II/1005)

data.turoyo: Kito maṯle ġalabe maʕ ʕame ḥrene, gədmaydono maṯlo as swedoye, i naqqa ban 1800 d azzənyo l ʕAmariqa, məlyon d swedoye, uʕdo, adyawma lə kəmmi, lə kmaḥisi ruḥayye wala an naʕimaṯṯe, lə kmətyaqnono an naʕime dan naʕimaṯṯe d maḥisi ruḥayye swedoye aw d kuḏʕi xabro swedoyo.
data.translation: There are many examples from other peoples. I shall take the Swedes as an example: when in the 1800s a million Swedes went to America, now, today they do not say, they do not feel themselves, nor their children, I do not believe their children's children feel themselves Swedish or know a Swedish word.

rationale: Self-identification subsense 2b with overt ruḥayye swedoye; one source context covers both repeated feel tokens.

summary: III alternates noncausative waking with transitive awakening: Preterit l-series indexes the experiencer in waking and the awakener in causative uses. 69/336 contains both within one quotation.

Bare negative forms during sleep can mean failure to wake or to notice; a free German rendering does not decide the Turoyo sense. ʕal- itself can also mark a waking trigger, as in MAC NE Mar Dumet/20.
The lebo phrase at 24/87 is already recorded verbatim in the entry's notes; retain it without creating a duplicate idiom.
Prym–Socin maḥaṣle/maḥəṣle and Ritter maḥiṣət are preserved with ṣ. No normalization to s or competing mḥs root is warranted by the local contexts.

Jan English is project machine translation [MT]. The causative reading of the question at 2.7/1820 is not adopted from its English: plural maḥəsse and the earlier plural people favour their awareness of what the government would do.

The Preterit l-series indexes a noncausative experiencer in noticing/waking, but III.5 has an awakener/informer and affected -lan. This distinction depends on local argument structure, not the translated verb alone.
Infectum-wa is absent from the original and round-1 boxes. Jan supplies plural, second-person feminine and conditional uses; -wa does not imply habit in every context.
Existing plus round-1 Preterit and Infectum cells for senses 1–3 are already full. No routine Jan examples are added merely because readers counted only the original entry.

The alert-state participle is retained in its inherited Detransitive Part. Pass. box, following the round-1 sense-1 correction; no new morphological box is inferred. The four earlier awake-state examples plus the distinctive plural warning provide five.

The self-experience construction groups comparative self-description, implicit self-membership and overt ruḥo with nationality/membership predicates. It is distinct from b-ruḥe sense 4: the reflexive here is the perceived self, not concealment or pretending. No idiom is added in parallel.

Some Jan prose is editorial discussion of interviews and language/identity, and some is quoted conversation. The cognitive/self-identification range should be reported across those contexts, without calling every occurrence learned written language.
Is awake-state maḥiso Part act. rather than the inherited Detransitive Part. Pass.? Can teḥiso be classified morphologically without implying a finite Detransitive paradigm?
At JTM 1.2/16 is du nsan an experiencer genitive, or could the nominal mean awakening the person? Cognitive content favors awareness, but agent/patient coding needs confirmation.
Collate 6/31: supplied Turoyo contains only causative kmaḥəsla, while the entry additionally quotes k-maḥiso i=ʕamṯo. Is the latter from another version?
Confirm ṣ/s variation and singular-looking maḥaṣle with coordinated participants in PrS 22/17; explain -lan in 6/32.
Does 112/183 ʕal ag garme describe bodily feeling or an idiomatic recovery of consciousness? No new idiom is established from this single ambiguous token.

Confirm whether lə maḥəsse i ḥkume at Jan 2.7/1820 means the earlier people did not notice what the government intended, or the government did not warn them. Only the first is provisionally assigned; no example is published.
Is awake/vigilant maḥiso morphologically Part act. rather than inherited Detransitive Part. Pass.? Do the stimulus-bearing states need a separate cognitive state description after editorial review?
At Jan 2.10/2734 are the Syriacs the experiencers? At Jan 1.51/2493 where does the subject switch from animals to people?
Does Jan 1.8/337 ask an emotional reaction or the manner of becoming aware? What precise recovery is expressed with oxyay at 3.11/117?
Clarify the secondary reference 69/415
rationale: 69/415 says the boy left nobody awake (lo ṭrele ḥa maḥiso), whereas the quoted sentence concerns the fox approaching a man who is awake with his eyes closed. The supplied PrS 75/6 matches that full sentence. Existing prs 217/35 may already identify the quotation in the entry’s pagination; 69/415 may intentionally be an additional attestation of maḥiso. Clarify its status rather than substitute the automatic match blindly.

summary: Use the base form hear after did not
rationale: Both alternatives governed by “did not” require the base form: notice or hear. Preserve the parenthetical alternative.

summary: Restore the missing n in ihn
rationale: “ih” is a truncated object pronoun. The supplied edition translation reads “packte ihn zudem”.

summary: Correct Als es nacht wurden
rationale: Nacht is a noun, and singular “es” takes “wurde”. The supplied edition translation has “Als es Nacht wurde”.

summary: Awake-state maḥiso is semantically related to waking/coming to consciousness. Inherited Detransitive Part. Pass. placement is provisional, not evidence of a passive event.
Perception targets include people, events, one's predicament and one's body; ʕal- and b- alternate, while an omitted stimulus is also frequent.
Metaphorical recovery after an ordeal remains an extension of coming to consciousness, with the relief interjection left uninterpreted.
Alert/vigilant maḥiso/maḥise supports round 1’s reassignment of awake-state examples away from sense 4. Its inherited Detransitive Part. Pass. position remains a morphological question.
Jan finite cognition with d- content and b-/ʕal- targets supports the cognitive domain of round-1 Detransitive Infinitiv sense 2 without repeating that nominal proposal.
